content: {"decision":"Unsafe as proposed: lease expiry proves loss of ownership, not that the provider did no work.","risks":["Automatic retry can duplicate output, charges, or side effects.","The original worker may still complete; stale writes can overwrite a retry's result.","A crash after provider success but before saving leaves an ambiguous outcome."],"required_changes":["Persist attempt identity and dispatch intent before calling the provider; record provider identifiers and results durably when available.","Move expired dispatched attempts to an outcome-unknown state, not ready. Retry automatically only when non-dispatch or failure without effects is established.","Reconcile using provider status, output lookup, or callbacks where available. If ambiguity cannot be resolved, require explicit acceptance of duplicate risk or manual resolution.","Use lease generations and conditional writes to fence stale workers. Preserve late results against their original attempt and select one canonical result atomically; fencing does not prevent duplicate provider execution.","Define bounded retries and compensation or deduplication for downstream effects. Exactly-once provider execution cannot be guaranteed without provider cooperation."],"evidence_needed":["Provider guarantees for status lookup, callbacks, cancellation, output retention, and billing.","Durable attempt records establishing whether dispatch occurred and linking any provider output.","Fault-injection tests covering crashes before dispatch, after provider completion but before persistence, lease expiry during execution, and late results racing recovery.","Explicit product policy accepting or rejecting duplicate work and charges when outcomes remain unknown."]}
